title: Memory-Aware Reward Modeling: Learning Human Preferences for LLM Memory Use
abstract: arXiv:2610.31272v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Memory enables language model assistants to maintain continuity across sessions and generate personalized responses, but knowing more about a user does not necessarily produce responses they prefer. Existing evaluations assess memory capabilities without directly establishing whether memory use benefits the user. To study this gap, we collect approximately 1,000 pairwise judgments from 87 participants using their own ChatGPT queries and personal memories. We find that memory-conditioned responses are not consistently preferred over responses generated without memory and in some cases, users strongly prefer the latter. Automatic evaluators also show limited agreement with users and favor memory-conditioned responses substantially more often than users do. Motivated by these gaps, we introduce a memory-aware reward model that learns from user judgments, achieving 72.8\% preference prediction accuracy and outperforming the existing baseline

translated_title: 记忆感知奖励建模：学习人类对大语言模型记忆使用的偏好
translated_abstract: 记忆使语言模型助手能够在会话之间保持连续性并生成个性化回复，但更多了解用户并不一定能生成用户更偏好的回复。现有评估方法仅评估记忆能力，而未直接确认记忆的使用是否真正让用户受益。为了研究这一空白，我们收集了来自87名参与者、基于他们自己的ChatGPT查询和个人记忆的大约1,000条成对偏好判断。我们发现，基于记忆条件生成的回复并不总是比不带记忆生成的回复更受用户偏好，某些情况下用户甚至强烈偏好后者。自动评估器与用户的一致性也很有限，且明显比用户更频繁地偏好基于记忆的回复。基于这些差距，我们提出了一种从用户判断中学习的记忆感知奖励模型，实现了72.8%的偏好预测准确率，并超越了现有基线方法。
tldr: 该研究通过对87名用户约1000条真实偏好判断的分析，首次揭示了大语言模型使用记忆并不总能生成用户偏好的回复，并提出了一种记忆感知奖励模型，以72.8%的准确率预测用户对记忆使用的偏好，填补了记忆评估领域的空白。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that memory use in LLM assistants does not consistently yield user-preferred responses, and introduces a memory-aware reward model trained on ~1,000 human pairwise judgments that achieves 72.8% preference prediction accuracy, outperforming existing baselines.
